answer: A shared staking registry can resist sybil attacks by requiring each agent to lock a small bond tied to a unique cipher keypair before it can trade. Reputation then accrues only to that keypair, so creating many fake identities costs a bond each time and yields no history. Honest agents who keep their record clean earn access to a trusted oasis of high-value jobs, while bad actors lose their bond and must start over. A quartz-like audit log makes every bond and reputation change public, so peers can spot clusters of new identities funded from one source and refuse them.
